I Understand Home Research Clinical Trials Clinical Trials .entry-header --> Clinical Trials The medical and surgical diagnostic tests and treatments of animals are similar to those in human medicine. In order to advance knowledge, researchers and clinicians at the College of Veterinary Medicine perform studies that investigate new diagnostics and treatments. These discoveries can often be applied to medicine across all species. Most clinical trials are based on preliminary laboratory research data that indicate that the new approach is better than what is already available. CASTR Alliance Skip to content Menu Home Mission Services Team News Testimonials Contact |Accelerating medical discovery | Advancing veterinary care CASTR: Companion Animal Studies for Translational Research Ongoing Studies Contact What we do CASTR Alliance aims to advance human and veterinary medicine by facilitating the discovery of innovative treatments through the management of high-quality veterinary clinical studies and collaboration with industry leaders and veterinary hospitals. We provide turnkey management of sponsored veterinary clinical studies to pharmaceutical and medical device development teams worldwide. We partner with state-of-the-art veterinary specialty and referral hospitals throughout the Pacific Northwest and beyond to enroll patients on sponsored clinical studies. We manage sponsored clinical trials that abide by Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards for veterinary studies and are designed to ensure the collection of high-quality data. We submit all CASTR-run studies for ethical review by an external Veterinary Clinical Studies Committee (VCSC) to prioritize the safety and well-being of all patients. The prognosis for DCM is often poor, with a less than 50% survival rate one year after clinical signs develop, unless a reversible underlying cause is identified. There is no available cure for Dilated Cardiomyopathy, current techniques focus on extending survival time as long as possible. However the focus of this clinical trial is to evaluate a potential curative treatment for cardiomyopathy in the Doberman Pinscher.
